Quase lá! A fração está entre 0 e 1, e o denominador é 4. O numerador é maior que 1, mas menor que 4. Pense: quantos quartos de hora tem meia hora?

Pense: se a unidade está dividida em 4 partes iguais, onde ficaria a segunda parte? Onde você pararia se contasse duas dessas partes a partir do zero?

Muito bem! 2/4 fica exatamente na metade da reta. Procure o ponto central entre 0 e 1 — ele corresponde a duas das quatro partes.

Read the fraction in the sentence about how long Sarah had to park.
Use the fraction connected to 30 minutes, not the earlier 15-minute example.
Copy the two numbers that appear on the two sides of the slash in the 30-minute statement.

misconceptions.description: Aluno rejeita a fração explícita e recalcula usando conhecimento de tempo
misconceptions.feedback: You converted 30 minutes into 30/60, but the problem already gives the requested fraction. Look for the fraction stated for the 30-minute parking time.

misconceptions.description: Aluno vincula erroneamente o valor em minutos ao denominador da fração
misconceptions.feedback: You connected 15 minutes to the denominator. The number 15 belongs to the first example; the requested fraction for 30 minutes is written separately.

misconceptions.description: Aluno lê '2/4' mas digita 4 no numerador e 2 no denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You reversed the two parts of the fraction. Read the fraction in the same order that it appears in the sentence.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator of the fraction for 30 minutes in f1.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator of the fraction for 30 minutes in f1.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many equal parts are being considered.
Locate the fraction for 30 minutes and look at the number before the slash.
The numerator is entered in the upper box, f1.
Type the number that comes before the slash in the fraction for 30 minutes.

misconceptions.description: Aluno lê '2/4' mas digita 4 no numerador e 2 no denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the denominator in the numerator box. The numerator is the number above the slash.

misconceptions.description: Aluno rejeita a fração explícita e recalcula usando conhecimento de tempo
misconceptions.feedback: You used the number of minutes instead of reading the fraction. The numerator must come from the fraction written in the problem.

misconceptions.description: Aluno vincula erroneamente o valor em minutos ao denominador da fração
misconceptions.feedback: You used the first parking time. Focus on the fraction associated with Sarah's 30-minute parking time.

nodes.description: Enter the denominator of the fraction for 30 minutes in f2.
nodes.instruction: Enter the denominator of the fraction for 30 minutes in f2.

hints.message: The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.
Find the fraction for 30 minutes and look at the number after the slash.
The denominator belongs in the lower box, f2.
Type the number below the slash in the fraction for 30 minutes.

misconceptions.description: Aluno mantém o denominador do primeiro exemplo (15 minutos → 1/4, mas interpreta erroneamente como 'denominador = 15') e só dobra o numerador
misconceptions.feedback: You treated 15 minutes as the denominator. The denominator is the number of equal parts in the hour, not the number of minutes in one part.

misconceptions.description: Aluno rejeita a fração explícita e recalcula usando conhecimento de tempo
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the parking time instead of the denominator. Read the number below the slash in the stated fraction.

misconceptions.description: Aluno identifica corretamente o numerador (2), mas falha ao associar o denominador, usando um número do contexto (ex: 15, 30, 60) em vez do 4
misconceptions.feedback: You repeated the numerator. The denominator is the other number in the fraction and goes in the lower box.

nodes.description: Type the numerator in the upper fraction box f1.
nodes.instruction: Type the numerator in the upper fraction box f1.

hints.message: Remember that the numerator is the number of selected parts.
Read the fraction for 30 minutes from left to right.
The upper box is for the number before the slash.
Enter the first number in the written fraction into f1.

misconceptions.description: Aluno lê '2/4' mas digita 4 no numerador e 2 no denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You placed the denominator in the upper box. The upper box holds the numerator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno rejeita a fração explícita e recalcula usando conhecimento de tempo
misconceptions.feedback: You entered minutes instead of the numerator. Use the fraction explicitly given for 30 minutes.

misconceptions.description: Aluno vincula erroneamente o valor em minutos ao denominador da fração
misconceptions.feedback: You used the first time value. The numerator must come from the fraction for the second parking time.

nodes.description: Type the denominator in the lower fraction box f2.
nodes.instruction: Type the denominator in the lower fraction box f2.

hints.message: The denominator counts the equal parts in the whole hour.
Find the number below the slash in the fraction connected to 30 minutes.
The lower box f2 is reserved for the denominator.
Enter the second number in the written fraction into f2.

misconceptions.description: Aluno mantém o denominador do primeiro exemplo (15 minutos → 1/4, mas interpreta erroneamente como 'denominador = 15') e só dobra o numerador
misconceptions.feedback: You used 15 as the denominator. The denominator describes the equal parts of an hour, not the first parking duration.

misconceptions.description: Aluno rejeita a fração explícita e recalcula usando conhecimento de tempo
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the number of minutes. The denominator is read from the fraction written in the problem.

misconceptions.description: Aluno identifica corretamente o numerador (2), mas falha ao associar o denominador, usando um número do contexto (ex: 15, 30, 60) em vez do 4
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the numerator again. The denominator is the number below the slash.

nodes.description: Mark 2/4 on the number line from 0 to 1.
nodes.instruction: Mark 2/4 on the number line from 0 to 1.

hints.message: Use the denominator to determine how many equal intervals the whole must have.
Count equal steps from 0 toward 1, with each step worth one fourth.
The first mark is 1/4, so the next mark is the one you need.
Starting at 0, move two equal intervals to the right and place the point there.

misconceptions.description: Aluno marca a posição correta do valor equivalente, mas ignora que o problema pede explicitamente a representação de 2/4, não de sua forma simplificada
misconceptions.feedback: The point at 0.5 has the same value as 2/4, but the requested representation uses four equal parts. Mark the second fourth.

misconceptions.description: Aluno comete erro de off-by-one ao contar intervalos vs. marcas | Aluno fixa na primeira fração citada e repete a marcação | Aluno fixa na primeira fração citada e repete a marcação
misconceptions.feedback: The first mark after zero is 1/4. Move one more equal interval to reach 2/4. (Ou, se foi por outro motivo: You marked the first example's location. Sarah parked twice as long, so the new point must be farther from zero.) (Ou, se foi por outro motivo: You marked the first example's location. misconceptions.description: Aluno estima a posição com base numa fração incorreta (2/15), levando a uma localização muito à esquerda
misconceptions.feedback: A point near zero represents a very small fraction. Count the four equal intervals and choose the second one.

nodes.description: Use the number line to show that 2/4 is less than 1.
nodes.instruction: Use the number line to show that 2/4 is less than 1.

hints.message: Compare the fraction's point with the endpoint labeled 1.
A fraction is less than 1 when its point appears before 1 on the number line.
The numerator is smaller than the denominator, so the point should remain inside the interval from 0 to 1.
Keep the point at the second of the four equal intervals, before the endpoint 1.

misconceptions.description: Aluno estima a posição com base numa fração incorreta (2/15), levando a uma localização muito à esquerda
misconceptions.feedback: A point at zero is not the fraction requested. Use the second of four equal parts, which is still before 1.

misconceptions.description: Aluno fixa na primeira fração citada e repete a marcação
misconceptions.feedback: The point for 1/4 is the first mark. The target is two equal parts from zero.

misconceptions.description: Aluno marca a posição correta do valor equivalente, mas ignora que o problema pede explicitamente a representação de 2/4, não de sua forma simplificada
misconceptions.feedback: Although 0.5 has the same value, keep the fraction represented as 2/4 on the four-part number line.

nodes.description: Convert 2/4 to a mixed number using Convert.
nodes.instruction: Convert 2/4 to a mixed number using Convert.

hints.message: A mixed number has a whole-number part and a fractional part.
Compare the numerator and denominator to determine how many complete wholes fit.
Because the numerator is smaller than the denominator, no complete whole is formed.
Use Convert, then enter zero in the whole-number box m1 while keeping the fractional part.

misconceptions.description: Aluno estima a posição com base numa fração incorreta (2/15), levando a uma localização muito à esquerda
misconceptions.feedback: You entered one whole, but 2/4 does not contain a complete whole because the numerator is smaller than the denominator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno lê '2/4' mas digita 4 no numerador e 2 no denominador
misconceptions.feedback: The whole-number part is not obtained by switching the numerator and denominator. Compare 2 with 4 to find how many complete wholes fit.
